issues.title: Missing semicolons in variable declarations
issues.description: The rule requires all JavaScript and TypeScript statements to end with explicit semicolons, but lines 88-90 rely on automatic semicolon insertion (ASI) instead

issues.title: Missing dependency in useEffect causes stale clamp detection
issues.description: The CommentContent component's useEffect hook has an empty dependency array, but it uses item.html to determine if content should be clamped. When a comment's HTML content changes (e.g., after an edit or when new data is loaded), the clamp detection won't re-run. This means the 'Show more' button may appear when it shouldn't or disappear when it should still be visible, creating a poor user experience. The dependency array should include item.html to ensure the clamp detection re-runs whenever the content changes.

issues.title: Filter button becomes non-functional when onAddFilter is undefined
issues.description: The conditional check for rendering the post title button was changed from `item.post?.id && item.post?.title && onAddFilter` to `item.post?.id && item.post?.title`, removing the onAddFilter null check. However, the button's onClick handler still calls onAddFilter('post', item.post!.id). Since onAddFilter is now a required prop in the TypeScript signature but the runtime check was removed, if onAddFilter is ever undefined or null at runtime, clicking the post title button will throw an error and crash the component. The original three-part condition was protecting against this scenario.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.id && item.post?.title ? ( ) : ( Unknown post )}

issues.title: Inconsistent conditional rendering pattern for feature image
issues.description: The feature image rendering logic was changed from a ternary expression with explicit null return (`condition ? : null`) to a logical AND operator (`condition && `). While functionally similar in most cases, this creates an inconsistency: when item.post?.feature_image is falsy (like an empty string ''), the logical AND will render the falsy value (empty string) instead of rendering nothing. This could lead to unexpected DOM nodes or React warnings. The original ternary with explicit null was more defensive and clearer about the intent to render nothing when the condition is false.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.feature_image && ( )}

issues.title: Delete comment functionality completely removed from UI
issues.description: The PR removes the dropdown menu item that allowed users to delete comments, making the delete functionality completely inaccessible through the UI. While all the backend infrastructure remains intact (AlertDialog component, confirmDelete function, deleteComment mutation, commentToDelete state), there is no button or menu item that calls setCommentToDelete to trigger the deletion flow. This is a critical functional regression that removes an essential moderation capability for administrators. Users can no longer delete comments through the interface, even though the API endpoint and confirmation dialog are still present in the code.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: {item.post?.url && ( View post )} {item.member?.id && ( View member )}

issues.title: Missing semicolons in CommentContent hook declarations
issues.description: The added variable/state declarations rely on automatic semicolon insertion (ASI). The codebase rule requires explicit semicolons at the end of all statements.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25745 - Redesigned comment moderation list layout

structured_output.summary:
This PR changes the admin comment moderation view from a five-column table to a feed-style list. Each row now shows an author/avatar line, a relative timestamp with a tooltip, a link to the post, comment HTML clamped to two lines with Show more/less, Hide/Show buttons, reply/like/report counts and an overflow menu. On the backend, `feature_image` is added to the comment serializer's `postFields` so the list can show a post thumbnail, and the API snapshots are updated to match.

The serializer change is small and safe. The frontend rewrite has problems, though. The "Delete comment" menu item was dropped, but the delete confirmation dialog and mutation were kept, so delete can no longer be reached from the UI. The new `CommentContent` keeps its clamp and expand state per virtual-row index, so the state goes stale when the list changes. That happens often, because clicking an author or post name now filters the list. Passing the optional `count` values to `formatNumber(value: number)` will probably fail the strict `tsc` step in `apps/posts`' build script.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Removing the delete action leaves the confirmation dialog as dead code and takes away a core moderation feature. On top of that, the clamp state is stale under virtualization and there's a likely strict-mode type error in a package whose build runs `tsc`.

architecture.overview:
The Comments view (`apps/posts/src/views/comments/comments.tsx`) gets comments through the infinite `useBrowseCommentsQuery` and passes them to `CommentsList`. `CommentsList` virtualizes the rows with `useInfiniteVirtualScroll`, a wrapper around TanStack Virtual whose row keys default to the item index. On the server, the admin comments endpoint serializes each comment through `mappers/comments.js`, which picks an allowlist of post fields from the related post.

The PR adds `feature_image` to that post allowlist and to the frontend `Comment` type. It then rebuilds each row as a two-cell table row. The first cell holds the meta line (author filter button, `formatTimestamp` with a tooltip, post filter button, hidden badge), a new stateful `CommentContent` component that measures line clamping, the Hide/Show action, the count indicators and a reduced dropdown (View post, View member). The second cell shows the post's feature image. `onAddFilter` is now a required prop, because the author and post names are themselves filter triggers.
steps: Start in `comments.tsx`: it fetches pages of comments and renders `CommentsList` with `handleAddFilter`.
On the server, `mappers/comments.js` now includes `feature_image` in `postFields`, so admin and members comment responses carry the post image URL.
`CommentsList` maps the virtual items from `useInfiniteVirtualScroll`. Each row's key is the virtual index, not the comment id.
Each row renders a meta line whose author and post buttons call `onAddFilter('author'|'post', id)`, which re-queries the list.
`CommentContent` renders the comment HTML with `line-clamp-2`, measures scrollHeight vs clientHeight on mount and resize, and toggles expansion.
The action bar has Hide/Show, reply/like/report counts (via `formatNumber`) and a dropdown with View post and View member. The delete item is gone, but the `AlertDialog` is still mounted.

findings.title: Delete action removed; delete confirmation dialog is now unreachable
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, the redesign removed the 'Delete comment' dropdown item (around lines 328-345), but `commentToDelete` state, `confirmDelete` and the `AlertDialog` (lines 149-157 and 366-384) are still there and can never open. Restore a destructive 'Delete comment' `DropdownMenuItem` inside the row's `DropdownMenuContent`, shown only when `item.status !== 'deleted'`, that calls `setCommentToDelete(item)`. Re-add `DropdownMenuSeparator` before it if you want the old visual separation. If removing delete was intentional, remove the dead `useDeleteComment` usage, state, `confirmDelete` and `AlertDialog` instead.

findings.title: CommentContent clamp/expand state is tied to the virtual index, so it goes stale when the list changes
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, `CommentContent` (lines 87-120) keeps `isClamped`/`isExpanded` state and measures clamping only on mount (`useEffect` with `[]`). Rows are keyed by virtual index (see `apps/posts/src/components/virtual-table/use-infinite-virtual-scroll.ts`, `key: virtualItem.key`), so when the item list changes (e.g. after `onAddFilter`), the state leaks to a different comment. Pass `key={item.id}` where `<CommentContent item={item} />` is rendered (line 261) so the state resets per comment. Also add `item.html` to the effect deps so clamping is re-measured when the content changes.

findings.title: formatNumber is called with possibly-undefined counts, which strict mode should reject
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, lines 281, 295 and 309 call `formatNumber(item.count?.replies)`, `formatNumber(item.count?.likes)` and `formatNumber(item.count?.reports)`. `formatNumber` (apps/shade/src/lib/utils.ts:252) takes a `number`, and the posts app compiles with `strict: true` via `tsc && vite build`, so `number | undefined` is a type error. Add `?? 0` to each argument. Then run `tsc` in apps/posts to confirm it passes.

findings.title: Resizing while expanded hides the 'Show less' button
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, `CommentContent` (lines 87-120) re-measures clamping on window resize. While expanded, the clamp class is removed, so `isClamped` becomes false and the 'Show less' button disappears. Change the render condition at line 114 to `(isClamped || isExpanded)`, or make `checkIfClamped` skip measuring while `isExpanded` is true.

findings.title: Conditional classes add a literal 'false' class and conflict with text-primary
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx`, several classNames use `${cond && 'class'}` template interpolation (lines 112, 194, 200, 279, 293). This emits a literal 'false' class, and on line 194 `text-primary` and `text-muted-foreground` conflict. Import `cn` from `@tryghost/shade` and rewrite these classNames with `cn(base, cond && 'class')` so falsy values are dropped and tailwind-merge resolves the colour conflict.

findings.title: Commented-out AvatarImage left in the row
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/posts/src/views/comments/components/comments-list.tsx` lines 200-207, the `AvatarImage` rendering is commented out. Either import `AvatarImage` from `@tryghost/shade` and render it when `item.member.avatar_image` is set (keeping `AvatarFallback` as the fallback), or remove the commented-out block.

findings.title: Serializer change is minimal and returns absolute image URLs
findings.body:
Adding `feature_image` to `postFields` is the smallest change that supports the thumbnail. The snapshots show the `__GHOST_URL__` fixture value coming out as an absolute URL, so the admin UI can use it directly. The members (public) comments API now returns it as well. That's fine because it's already-public post data, and the activity-feed content-length snapshots were updated to match.
